# effect-spacetimedb 0.7.0

The first release since 0.6.0, and a breaking one. Public options, fields and
error members move to a qualifier-last spelling; the required `spacetimedb` peer
moves to `~2.10.1`, which brings upstream's camelCase generated accessors and
its function-side schedule registration; field annotations gain an enforced
version boundary, so two copies of this package in one dependency tree now fail
explicitly instead of misreading each other's fields; and the client gains typed
connection loss, supervised sessions, invalidation observation and grouped HTTP
namespaces. The migration checklist below covers everything that needs an edit
in your code.

## Breaking changes

### Migrating from 0.6

#### 1. Rename the qualifier-last identifiers

Identifiers owned by this package now put the most significant word first and
qualifiers (`default`, `max`, `min`, `first`, `last`, …) last. Four spellings
are reachable from the public API:

| Before | After | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `defaultServerRuntimeMode` | `serverRuntimeModeDefault` | exported from `effect-spacetimedb/server` |
| `lastSnapshotSize` | `snapshotSizeLast` | field of `WaitUntilTimeoutError` (`effect-spacetimedb/client`) |
| `defaultValue` | `valueDefault` | normalized field options: `FieldOptionsOf<…>`, `FieldType`, and the field annotation payload |
| `firstPublish` | `publishFirst` | `clear.firstPublish` option of `effect-spacetimedb/dev-server` |

Two things did *not* change and need no edit: the `default` you write when
declaring a column — `.default(value)` and the `{ default: value }` option form
are both untouched, only the *normalized* option is spelled `valueDefault` — and
every SATS type name, table name, column name and reducer argument name. Nothing
on the wire moved, so a 0.7.0 client and a 0.6.0 module still speak the same
protocol.

The remaining renames are internal locals with no public binding site. If you
only use documented API, the table above is the complete list.

#### 2. Move the `spacetimedb` peer to `~2.10.1`, and match your CLI to it

```sh
npm install effect-spacetimedb@0.7.0 spacetimedb@2.10.1 effect@4.0.0-rc.117
```

The `effect` and `@effect/atom-react` peers move from `^4.0.0-beta.93` to
`^4.0.0-rc.117`, and that floor is real rather than cautious. Effect
`4.0.0-rc.113` renamed `SchemaGetter.transformOrFail` to `transformEffect` and
`4.0.0-rc.116` reshaped `SchemaGetter.Getter`; 0.7.0 is written against, and
tested on, `4.0.0-rc.117`. Any later 4.0.0 release candidate, and 4.0.0 itself
once it is cut, satisfies the caret; anything older is a version this package
has never been run on.

That same rc.113 rename is why **0.6.0 cannot be loaded at all on
`effect >= 4.0.0-rc.113`**: its `dist/schema-transform.js` calls
`SchemaGetter.transformOrFail` while the module is being evaluated, so importing
it throws `TypeError: SchemaGetter.transformOrFail is not a function` before any
of its API is reachable. A published tarball cannot be changed, so that is
permanent — and it bounds what section 4 below describes. The explicit
annotation-version error is the failure you see when *both* copies can load,
which is only on the `4.0.0-rc.110`-`4.0.0-rc.112` window. On `4.0.0-rc.113`
and later, a dependency tree that still holds a 0.6.0 copy fails earlier and
more bluntly, the moment that copy is imported.

0.6.0 required `spacetimedb` 2.6.x. 0.7.0 requires `~2.10.1`, and the `spacetime`
CLI you generate and publish with **must be the same version as the SDK you
install**. This is not a style preference: the module definition emitted by an
SDK is patch-coupled to the host that accepts it — SDKs from 2.8.0 onward always
emit a `Submodules` section that older hosts reject — so a split pin fails at
publish time rather than at compile time. Pin both explicitly, and move both
together.

#### 3. Regenerate your generated clients

Upstream 2.10 changed the shape of generated bindings: accessor keys on a
generated client's `db` are camelCase. Tables and views are resolved by their
contract key, which is that camelCase accessor key, and that is the only
spelling resolved — the deprecated snake_case aliases upstream still emits are
never looked up.

Regenerate every checked-in generated client with the 2.10.1 CLI before
upgrading. A client generated by an older CLI exposes the old accessor keys and
will not resolve against a 0.7.0 contract.

#### 4. Install exactly one copy of `effect-spacetimedb`

Column options are carried on the schema as an annotation under a global key.
0.6.0 wrote that payload unversioned, which meant two different copies of this
package in one dependency tree could silently misread each other's fields —
each one seeing a payload it did not write and taking the parts it recognized.

0.7.0 versions the payload and enforces the boundary. A field annotated by an
incompatible copy — an older unversioned annotation, or a payload version this
copy does not know — is no longer silently accepted: reading it fails with an
explicit typed error naming both the version that wrote the annotation and the
version reading it. The fix is always the same: deduplicate
`effect-spacetimedb` so exactly one copy is installed (`npm ls
effect-spacetimedb`, `npm dedupe`, or a resolution pin), then rebuild.

One direction cannot be fixed from here: a **0.6.0** copy reading a field
annotated by 0.7.0 does not recognize the new key and therefore sees no field
options at all — no primary key, no unique, no index, no default. Published
0.6.0 has no boundary check to trigger. If you upgrade, upgrade every copy.

All of this is only observable where both copies can load, which — per section
2 — means `effect@4.0.0-rc.112` and older. On the `4.0.0-rc.117` this release
requires, a leftover 0.6.0 copy throws on import instead, so the remedy is the
same and you meet it sooner.

#### 5. Ranges over a full-width composite key now work

0.6.0 rejected a range whose bound covered every column of a composite key,
because upstream dispatched such a scan as a point lookup. Upstream fixed the
point-versus-range dispatch and the prefix arithmetic in 2.10, so the guard is
gone: a range in the final column of a full-width composite key is now a normal,
supported scan. If you worked around the old rejection by widening a query and
filtering in memory, you can delete that workaround.

## New

- **Sum- and enum-typed keys and index members.** A sum or enum column may now
  be a primary key and may participate in an index, which upstream 2.10 allows.
- **Scheduled functions register through `onSchedule`.** Scheduling is now
  declared on the function rather than through the deprecated table-side
  `scheduled` option. The authoring surface of this package is unchanged —
  `scheduledTable(...)` and your scheduled reducers and procedures are written
  exactly as before — but the registration it emits is the current one, so
  scheduled modules keep working on a 2.10 host.
- **Typed connection loss.** A WebSocket reducer, procedure or view call that
  races connection death now fails with `ConnectionLostError` carrying the
  cause, instead of hanging or resolving against a dead session. Treat it as an
  unknown outcome: it does not prove the call was never applied.
- **Supervised WebSocket sessions.** `wsSupervisor`, `wsSupervisorFromModulePlan`
  and `wsSupervisorGenerated` build a scoped supervisor that bounds activation,
  retries with capped jittered backoff (`reconnectDelayMillisFirstDefault`,
  `reconnectDelayMillisMaxDefault`), re-establishes declared subscriptions, and
  publishes a connecting/live/reconnecting/fatal phase you can render. A
  supervisor defect surfaces as a typed fatal phase
  (`WsSessionSupervisorDefectError`) rather than a silently dead background
  fiber, and a previously live session is retained as waiting so read models can
  keep showing stale data. `supervisedSessionAtom` in
  `effect-spacetimedb/client/atom` adapts a handle for atom consumers. Bare
  sessions keep their previous semantics; this is opt-in.
- **Invalidation observation.** Sessions expose `awaitInvalidation()`,
  `isInvalidated()` and `observeInvalidation(...)`. These report connection-level
  death only; an individual query-set rejection stays scoped to the stream, ref
  or atom that owns it.
- **HTTP group namespaces.** Each authored group is exposed as a typed namespace
  on the HTTP client (`client.Users.reducers.…`), and
  `Example.client.http.group("Users", config)` builds one group's client on its
  own. Group views are lazy and identity-preserving: every grouped member is the
  same function object as its flat counterpart, including `.raw`. The flat
  surface is unchanged.

Also in this release: filtered native subscriptions, connection snapshot atoms,
timestamp helpers, complete subscription handles, and the post-handshake
disconnect semantics of 2.10 (a socket error after the handshake now arrives as
a disconnect with a cause rather than as a connect error).

## Known upstream issues

These are defects in the `spacetimedb` package itself as of 2.10.1, confirmed
still present upstream as of 2026-09-18. They are listed here
because their symptoms are easy to mistake for a fault in this package.
`effect-spacetimedb` does not shim them.

1. **A `Result` value whose `err` payload type differs from its `ok` payload
   type is serialized with the `ok` encoder.** The decoder reads `err` with the
   correct type, so the two halves of the codec disagree. Nothing throws at
   encode time; the payload is simply written wrong and the read side then fails
   or returns nonsense — encoding `{ err: "boom" }` for a
   `Result<u8, string>` writes a single zero byte and decoding it raises a
   `RangeError`. Avoid by giving `ok` and `err` the same payload type, or by
   carrying the error as a sum type in the `ok` position, until upstream fixes
   it.
2. **A btree index on a proper subset of a composite unique constraint's
   columns is built as a unique accessor.** Given a unique constraint on
   `(tenant, email)` and a btree index on `tenant` alone, the index is treated
   as unique: `filter` is missing (calling it is a `TypeError`), and `find`
   returns one arbitrary matching row instead of rejecting the query. Avoid by
   not indexing a strict prefix of a composite unique constraint, or by reading
   such an index through a full table scan until upstream fixes it.
3. **Client-cache range bounds compare incorrectly over `Identity`,
   `ConnectionId`, `Timestamp`, `TimeDuration` and `Uuid` columns.** The cache's
   comparator uses reference equality and relational operators on what are
   wrapper objects, so an `excluded` bound keeps the boundary row, an `included`
   bound can drop it, and for the three types without a string form the ordering
   itself is meaningless. There is no error — the scan silently returns the
   wrong rows. Avoid by ranging over the wrapped integer column directly, or by
   filtering the returned rows yourself, until upstream fixes it.
4. **`Prettify` flattens branded primitives and `Uuid`.** Every column type is
   passed through a helper meant to flatten intersections; wrapper types that
   are not intersections come back rewritten. A `t.uuid()` column infers as a
   structural record of `Uuid`'s members rather than as `Uuid`, which shows up
   as unreadable type errors and broken assignability. This is a types-only
   issue with no runtime effect; annotate the affected value explicitly to work
   around it.

## Tags

This is the first tagged release. Versions before 0.7.0 have no git tag, because
the commits they were built from are no longer part of this repository's
history.
